nodes.content: Design a distributed recursive-query engine that incrementally maintains cyclic reachability under concurrent insertions and deletions with snapshot-consistent reads.
requirements: Every committed snapshot matches least-fixed-point recomputation, including deletions that break or preserve cycles.
Pass 10,000 randomized concurrent update/read histories with worker crashes, without full-query recomputation after individual updates.

nodes.content: Use WAL-backed atomic MVCC epochs, distributed dynamic SCCs, and condensation-DAG reachability; repair only affected regions on deletion.
How can concurrent deletions split SCCs while restricting repair to affected regions and keeping epoch-pinned reads atomic?
Epoch-serialized conflicting edits, affected-SCC rebuilds, and atomic MVCC publication yield zero snapshot mismatches across 10,000 crash-injected histories.
Serialize conflicting batches into WAL epochs; repair SCC splits/merges and ancestor reachability; atomically publish MVCC; differential-test 10,000 crash-injected histories.
Implement WAL-ordered epoch batching, SCC-local split/merge repair, affected-ancestor DAG reachability refresh, and atomic MVCC publication.
ReachEpoch v0.1 implements WAL-replayed epoch commits, SCC-local repairs, ancestor reachability updates, and atomically published MVCC snapshots.
Run ReachEpoch v0.1 through 10,000 seeded concurrent crash histories; compare committed snapshots against independent least-fixed-point recomputation.
ReachEpoch v0.1: 10,000 crash-injected histories yielded zero committed-snapshot mismatches; incremental updates invoked zero full-query recomputations.
Adopt ReachEpoch v0.1’s incremental SCC repair: 10,000 crash-injected histories showed zero snapshot mismatches and no full-query recomputations.
Stress ReachEpoch v0.1 on CycleSplit-1M adversarial SCC deletions; measure touched vertices, p99 update latency, and snapshot equivalence.
CycleSplit-1M critical-edge deletions touched 940,000 vertices (94%), with 4.8-second p99 update latency and zero snapshot mismatches.
Affected-SCC repair touches under 10% of vertices and keeps p99 updates below 500 ms on CycleSplit-1M critical-edge deletions.
What locality and update-latency limits can affected-SCC repair meet on CycleSplit-1M critical-edge deletions?
Use strong-bridge certificates and range-compressed SCC splits to propagate batched reachability deltas before atomic epoch publication.
Build versioned bridge certificates with SCC-rebuild fallback; batch compressed DAG deltas, atomically publish epochs, and oracle-test 10,000 crash histories.
Extend ReachEpoch v0.1 with strong-bridge certificates and compressed splits; compare baseline latency and oracle correctness on CycleSplit-1M and crash histories.
CycleSplit-1M p99 fell from 4.8 s to 0.9 s; 10,000 crash histories showed zero mismatches or full-query update recomputations.
Bridge-certified splits keep CycleSplit-1M critical-edge deletion p99 below 1 s, without requiring a 10%-touch bound.
Run 30 fresh CycleSplit-1M seeds with critical-edge deletions; measure p99 update latency, touched vertices, and snapshot-oracle mismatches.
Across 30 CycleSplit-1M seeds, worst-seed p99 was 0.94 s; median vertex-touch rate was 91%, with zero snapshot mismatches.
Prefer bridge-certified splits over baseline SCC repair: worst-seed p99 fell below 1 s, despite 91% median vertex touches.
Implement ReachEpoch v0.2 with selected bridge-certified splits, SCC-rebuild fallback, WAL-persisted compressed deltas, and atomic MVCC epoch publication.
ReachEpoch v0.2 contains versioned bridge certificates, SCC-rebuild fallback, WAL-replayed compressed reachability deltas, and atomic MVCC epoch publication.
How can bridge-certified splits avoid stale certificates when concurrent insertions reconnect an SCC within the same epoch?
Validating bridge certificates against each epoch’s final edge set and rebuilding invalidated SCCs yields zero mismatches in 10,000 mixed-update histories.
Use MVCC-epoch differential dataflow with deletion-aware overdelete/rederive, sharded reachability witnesses, and distributed quiescence barriers.
How can sharded overdelete/rederive eliminate self-supporting cyclic witnesses while detecting global quiescence before publishing an MVCC epoch?
Prototype sharded overdelete/rederive atop ReachEpoch v0.2; test cyclic mixed updates, certificate validation, and quiescence against 10,000 crash-injected oracle histories.
With verified quiescence, final-edge-set certificate validation and invalidated-SCC rebuilds yielded four stale cross-shard snapshots in 10,000 mixed-update histories.
Epoch-fenced cross-shard certificate invalidation and quiescence-verified overdelete/rederive eliminate stale snapshots across 10,000 cyclic mixed-update crash histories.
Epoch-fence cross-shard invalidations; validate certificates against final edges, rebuild invalidated SCCs, then quiesce and oracle-test 10,000 histories.
Run 10,000 oracle-checked mixed-update crash histories on ReachEpoch v0.2, comparing final-edge validation with/without epoch-fenced invalidations after overdelete/rederive quiescence.
Globally sealed edge-set validation/rebuild: zero mismatches; epoch-fenced invalidation with verified quiescence: two stale snapshots in 10,000 crash histories.
Replay two stale-history seeds on ReachEpoch v0.2 with epoch-fenced invalidations; trace certificate versions, rederive messages, and publication order.
Both stale histories reused prior-epoch invalidation acknowledgments, prematurely sealing certificates; rederive quiescence remained correct, implicating incomplete epoch fencing.
Use globally sealed edge-set validation; reject current epoch-fenced invalidation until acknowledgments are epoch-tagged and retested.
Introduce consensus-sealed edge epochs with epoch-tagged invalidation acknowledgments and post-quiescence affected-SCC certificate validation before atomic MVCC publication.
Can epoch-tagged acknowledgments prevent premature certificate sealing without consensus-barrier delays exceeding 1-second p99 on CycleSplit-1M?
Epoch-tagged acknowledgments eliminate stale snapshots across 10,000 crash histories while keeping CycleSplit-1M p99 updates below 1 s.
Tag invalidation acknowledgments by epoch, gate certification on sealed-edge quiescence, then oracle-test crash histories and benchmark CycleSplit-1M p99.
Patch ReachEpoch v0.2 to reject prior-epoch acknowledgments and validate affected SCCs against sealed edges after distributed rederive quiescence.
ReachEpoch v0.3 adds epoch-tagged invalidation acknowledgments, sealed-edge SCC validation, post-quiescence certification, and atomic MVCC publication.
Test ReachEpoch v0.3 on 10,000 crash-injected update/read histories against a fixed-point oracle; benchmark CycleSplit-1M p99 update latency.
ReachEpoch v0.3: zero snapshot mismatches across 10,000 crash histories; CycleSplit-1M p99 updates 0.98 s, without full-query update recomputation.
Adopt ReachEpoch v0.3: epoch-tagged sealing yielded zero mismatches in 10,000 crash histories and 0.98-second CycleSplit-1M p99.
Shard source-rooted reachability forests with WAL-replayed epochs; repair deletion-invalidated branches via surviving alternate edges before atomic MVCC publication.
Implement versioned source-rooted forests; reattach invalidated branches from intact frontiers, seal WAL/MVCC epochs, and oracle-test 10,000 crash histories.
Prototype source-rooted forest repair atop ReachEpoch v0.3; compare both on 10,000 crash-history oracle checks and CycleSplit-1M p99.
Forest repair missed surviving alternate paths after seven cycle-preserving deletions in 10,000 crash histories; ReachEpoch v0.3 had zero mismatches.
Epoch-tagged sealing plus sealed-edge alternate-path validation should retain zero mismatches and subsecond CycleSplit-1M p99, unlike forest-only repair.
Add sealed-edge alternate-path checks to epoch-tagged acknowledgment handling; oracle-test 10,000 crash histories and benchmark CycleSplit-1M p99.
Instrument ReachEpoch v0.3 with sealed-edge alternate-path validation; replay failed forest seeds and 10,000 crash histories, then measure CycleSplit-1M p99.
Across 10,000 histories both variants had zero mismatches; CycleSplit-1M p99 was 0.98 s baseline versus 1.31 s with alternate-path checks.
Trace alternate-path validation overhead on CycleSplit-1M, separating bridge-certificate checks, sealed-edge probes, and MVCC publication.
CycleSplit-1M traces attributed 0.34 s to redundant sealed-edge probes; deduplicated trace replay projected 0.97 s p99.
Keep ReachEpoch v0.3 unchanged; treat probe deduplication as unverified until live p99 beats 1 s without snapshot mismatches.
Reject forest-only repair after seven missed paths; retain validated ReachEpoch v0.3 rather than unverified alternate-path optimization.
